q: I am lying in bed awake, in desperate need of sleep, thinking about how i let myself down today as a parent.
cx: Parent of a toddler and an infant after a hard bedtime.

q: Long rant, but I need someone to hear me. My husband and I live in a state with no family and zero friends.
cx: Mother of a 6.5-month-old with very low sleep needs; husband works 60–70 hour weeks.

q: I had to have him sleep on my chest for every sleep, every nap, every night. He would not sleep otherwise. I slept upright in excruciating pain every night.
I got 1-4 hours of severely shattered sleep per day. All of this was every. single. day. for 8 weeks straight. I was so sleep deprived.
I need solidarity. I need another mom to tell me they understand. This isn't just the same as any other baby. There is no magic cure. There is no perfect method needing only discovered.

the acid reflux is keeping me up at night and burning my throat all day, I’m barely sleeping with my bladder keeping me up at night (6-8x a night) and night sweats, and on top of it all when I ranted to my husband he said “just be positive, you’re being negative”.
That’s SO easy for other people to say when they’re not going through it! I just broke down and started sobbing and have been crying all morning.

I’m chasing him around all day and then I’m awake all night. I feel like I could collapse any day now. I’m also returning to work in a month. I don’t know how I will do it because I’m not sleeping at all.
cx: Alone with a 3-year-old and a nursing 6-month-old.

q: I cosleep with a 3 year old and 6 month old alone. I nurse my 6 month old all night long it feels like.

We have attempted to switch to ONLY my husband going in to hold her so that she understands there’s no more milk at night, but this arrangement is not going well because he cannot get back to sleep after going in/out and holding her for these short bursts
cx: Nearly 14-month-old waking at 1am for a month.

q: I really dont want to nurse her at night for so many reasons: its disruptive to me and usually means I won’t sleep for hours
My baby is clocking 8 hours of sleep a day at best. We are getting 4 hours at night at most.
cx: First-time mother at 39 of a 6-month-old who contact naps only.

q: So is this hopeless? Will it ever change? All of us need more sleep, but I simply don’t know what to do!
This sounds much less emotionally challenging (for me) than other forms of sleep training. Thank you so much for this.. probably something I will attempt when I have more reserve.
cx: Reply to a gentle method suggestion.

q: the first time around, I ended up doing most of the night shifts because of a combination of: 1) maternity leave, 2) husband got sick, 3) trying to breastfeed, 4) husband gets easily frustrated with baby and with a baby who refused to be put down, he would just leave her to cry it out, 5) husband really cannot handle sleep deprivation at all and sometimes won’t even wake up if the baby is screaming in the same room.
cx: Mother of a one-year-old weighing a second baby.

q: But I just don’t know how I will survive a second baby if we get another difficult baby.  We don’t have a lot of family support nearby.
Night nanny would help for the first couple months.. but doesn’t seem to make sense to use them after that initial period, though they’re not quite sleeping through the night yet
cx: Weighing paid help for a possible second baby.

q: And I think it was easier for me to just deal with it than to try to fight him on it when I was already so exhausted.
Baby is a month old and still waking every hour at night. Not during the day of course, he'll sleep 2-3 hours straight when I need to eat, or do laundry or be awake for my toddler.
cx: Breastfeeding mother of a newborn and a toddler.

q: My husband will take him after 5am Thankfully. But only on the weekends. I'm dreading the week ahead being sleep deprived with no respite for 5 days straight.

I have to be sparing with the bottle because I didn't get more than 3 feedings worth of milk pumped because my supply was low and I don't want to dip into my stash (but I will if it means I get some fucking sleep after 5am)
I'm tired of feeling so much dread and sadness at night and I'm tired of not getting enough sleep
when she said she was tired I said this: ‘just wait until you have that baby and get at least 2 hours of restful sleep. Oh my god it’s amazing.
cx: Parent of a 6-month-old describing what they told a pregnant relative.

q: Because in the crappiest moments where I’m cleaning up a massive poo at 3am on a screaming baby with bleary eyes, that little smile he gives me at 7 in the morning is what keeps me holding on to sanity.
40w 2 days. I’m so tired. Can’t sleep.
cx: Overdue, on maternity leave, mother visiting to help.

q: I used to wake up at 4:40am to wash my face, put on a little makeup, change my earrings, feed the cats, make coffee, do a 30-45min workout, maybe do one quick house chore, and wake baby up around 7am to leave for daycare at 8am but I was only able to do that for a month before I was too burned out. […] It felt amazing because I was finally making time for self care!!! But the cost was my sleep and sleep is self care too.
cx: Working mother of a 6-month-old who does chores until bedtime.

q: Then at the end of the night during the bedtime feed, I fall asleep feeding. My body is so exhausted by the end of the day, I literally cannot keep my eyes open.
we exclusively breast feed and he likes to nurse to sleep, but lately he wants to nurse ALL NIGHT and my sleep is so compromised from this.
cx: Stay-at-home mother of a 2-year-old and an 8-month-old.

q: Unfortunately that means bed for me at 8:30 right now to because if I even get up outta my bed and watch him in the monitor he gets up and cries as soon as he realizes I’m gone
cx: Her bedtime is set by the baby's.

q: Just an update he took both his naps on his own yesterday and it did take an hour last night and a few checking but baby boy slept ALL NIGHT in HIS bed 🤩

I’m 2.5 months postpartum, severely sleep deprived, pumping around the clock, trying to figure out breastfeeding, healing physically and mentally, and taking care of a newborn basically all day. My mom is here helping me, thank God, but she leaves at the end of this month and I’m already anxious about how I’ll manage alone.
My husband’s response was: “If you can’t do all this and if this is hard, why have a baby?”
cx: After she said the phase was hard.

q: Today he literally said he “can’t listen to all this” and walked out of the house mid-conversation.

Whenever I talk about how exhausting pumping is, he just says “then give formula.” But what I’m really looking for in those moments isn’t solutions — it’s comfort. Reassurance. Maybe even small acts of help when he can, like washing pump parts while I’m feeding the baby instead of scrolling on his phone.
The workload itself is hard, but feeling emotionally unsupported while doing it is what’s breaking me.

ever since i reached my third trimester i have NOT been able to sleep. normal. id only get maybe about 4 hours of sleep and mind you my kids are older and in school and im a sahm so normally while theyre in school thats my alone peace time.. i cant even take naps. ill be super tired, weak even but still cant sleep. so i got used to it.
cx: Thirty-four weeks, first pregnancy in seven years.

q: he complains about doing the night feeds when he does them 2-3 days a week and i do the rest. he’ll complain about being tired during the week when i havent slept for days.
cx: Nineteen, five weeks postpartum, living with her mother; the father stays at weekends.

q: yesterday he asked if i’ve ever had to cover my ears whilst the baby has been crying at night and i said no? because when hes crying at night its always for a feed so now im thinking he’s ignoring our babies feeding cues.
his dad messaged my mum telling her to lay off him and to let him enjoy being a new dad.
cx: After her mother sent him job listings.
